Exact complement/interior/closure identity in the same ambient metric space.

The same rational-domain E is the continuous square preimage of the open interval (2,3), hence relatively open in ℚ, not asserted closed in ℝ.

First digit forces x≥0.4; closedness excludes zero from closure. Both ambient [0,1] inclusion and subspace Dense formulations are negated.

A finer Polish topology makes the irrational complement closed; an injective continuous binary-space map into it is continuous in the usual topology as well. Its usual-real range is nonempty, perfect, compact, and disjoint from every rational. The chosen set retains all properties.
Disjoint closed A,B imply closure(A)∩B=∅ and A∩closure(B)=∅. separatedSets is exactly the source condition.
Disjoint open A,B satisfy the same separation condition; disjoint closures are not required or asserted.
Opposite strict sides of the distance level δ are disjoint open sets and hence separated. All real δ is a valid strengthening of source δ>0.

Preconnected metric space with explicit distinct a,b has continuous distance image containing [0,dist(a,b)]. Its positive length rules out Countable of the full space. Singleton/empty spaces are excluded by a≠b.

In Euclidean ℝ², {p:p₀≠0 or p=0} is star/path-connected; its interior is exactly the two open half-planes. Projection onto first coordinate proves this interior is not preconnected.
For the actual affine p(t)=(1−t)a+tb on all real t, continuous preimages of separated A,B are separated. Endpoint membership is unnecessary for this part and not added.
Endpoint membership a∈A,b∈B plus separation imply an actual t strictly between 0 and 1 outside A∪B. Compact-segment connectedness rules out coverage; endpoints are treated separately.

Arbitrary compact metric X has actual Countable dense subset, not merely an asserted typeclass without witness. Includes finite/empty X under the inventory convention.

P quantifies every open neighborhood with uncountable intersection with E, not only neighborhoods of members of E. Complement openness gives closedness; the countable remainder rules out isolated points. Applies to all second-countable spaces and hence the stated Euclidean case.

Countable basis refines each neighborhood with countable intersection; E\P lies in a countable union of countable intersections. Countable means finite or countably infinite, exactly the source remainder assertion.
Every closed F in a metric space with Countable dense D decomposes as Perfect P∪Countable C. No ambient completeness and no nonempty F/P assumption; equality ensures both pieces lie in F.

Closed Euclidean F with Countable AND Infinite matches Definition 2.4's countably-infinite meaning, giving an isolated member. It is not the false empty-set version and does not extend to arbitrary separable metrics.
Empty Euclidean set is closed and Countable but has no isolated member. This refutes an at-most-countable translation without nonemptiness, not the original strict-countability statement.

Closed, at-most-countable, nonempty Euclidean F has an isolated member: otherwise Perfect F embeds binary sequences, contradicting countability by diagonalization. Includes finite F and dimension zero.

Arbitrary open U is union of Countable pairwise disjoint nonempty open components under the explicitly defined four-shape convention. PDF287 supports unbounded segments; this is not a proof with finite endpoints only.

Open connected ℝ cannot be a pairwise disjoint union of bounded Ioo intervals, even with arbitrary index type and empty members. One nonempty member would be clopen and hence all ℝ, contradicting its finite endpoint.

Actual connectedComponentIn family includes only components through U. Countability, pairwise disjointness, nonemptiness, openness, preconnectedness, four interval shapes and exact union are proved. Empty U gives empty family; rays and ℝ have themselves as sole components.
